messages.subject: "X may not be of full rank in group 1"
parts:
Hello

Similar errors have been discussed in this forum earlier - however, none of the suggested solutions worked for me. Hence I am seeking out help. 

I have a model of the form

model1 <- ' Y1 ~ X1
                   Y2 ~ X2
                   Y1 ~~ Y2
'
Y1 and Y2 are ordinal variables. I get the parametric estimates etc. without any errors. 
fit <- sem(model1, data=analysisdata, debug = TRUE, missing = "pairwise")

I now added a third endogenous variable - a numeric variable. 
model1 <- ' Y1 ~ X1
                   Y2 ~ X2
                   Y3 ~ X3
                   Y1 ~~ Y2
                   Y3 ~~ Y2
'

This gives me the following error: Error in muthen1984(Data = X[[g]], ov.names = ov.names[[g]], ov.types = ov.types,  : 
  lavaan ERROR: linear regression failed for Y3; X may not be of full rank in group 1

Please note that 
(a) this is not a multi group analysis (with reference to "group 1" in the error message. 
(b) X3 is a subset of X2 - (with reference to the error X may not be of full rank)

Descriptive analysis of Y3 does not indicate anything out of the ordinary. 

Thanks a lot.

Yes, but lavaan thinks of this as a single-group analysis.

> (b) X3 is a subset of X2 - (with reference to the error X may not be of
> full rank)

I am not sure what you mean with subset. But it would seem that the 'X'
matrix (the columns X1, X2, X3) are not of full rank. Can you check
this? If this is the case, you need to remove one these three predictors.

Yves.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: "X may not be of full rank in group 1"
parts:
On 03/28/2016 07:30 AM, Gouri Shankar Mishra wrote:
> Hi Yves
>
> I did figure out the X variable that were responsible. I wonder if there
> is some way to identify the X easily - based on error messages from
> Lavaan or something else.

Well, what you could do is the following:

1) get the list of exogenous 'x' variables:

x.names <- lavNames(lavaanify(model1), "ov.x")

2) create the 'X' matrix:

X <- analysisdata[,x.names]

3) remove cases with missing values, make it a matrix:

X1 <- as.matrix(X[complete.cases(X),])

4) create the crossproduct matrix

XX <- crossprod(X1)

5) decompose the XX matrix using a pivoting method; 'chol' will do:

chol(XX)

which says:

Error in chol.default(XX) :
the leading minor of order 32 is not positive definite

So variable '32' is the culprit; in your dataset, this is

> x.names[32]
[1] "DLAge"

Removing this variable makes XX invertible.

Yves.
